traveler: Emilia Massacesi (Emilia Portman / Em Port / Emi Massa)
title: The Record That Begins in January 2015: a Licenciada in Choreographic Composition, and a Second Name on the Pole
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: West of the City, Before Any Record

stops.name: Zona oeste, the tutu and the Shakira costume
stops.date_confidence: undated childhood, given in her own words in the NewsDigitales/Living interview; no year, no month, no town. The pin sits on Morón as a conventional stand-in for 'el oeste,' which is all she names; an earlier pass placed the same claim near Moreno, some fourteen kilometres away, and neither point is attested.
stops.campa: She is small, visiting older cousins, and none of them dance. In a box of clothes she finds a costume tutu, puts it on, and will not give it back. 'Acá hay una data,' she says of that moment much later, and she is taken to a dance class soon afterward. She sets a second memory beside that one rather than behind it, and gives neither of them a year or a town. The second is a birthday party somewhere in the 2000s: a Shakira costume, a child dancing salvajemente, no training in Arabic dance whatsoever.
stops.quote: ¿Cómo llegó la danza a mi vida? Creo que a través de un tutú.
stops.quote_source: Emilia Massacesi, NewsDigitales/Living interview (host Marisol), transcript
suggested_refs: The NewsDigitales/Living long-form interview, her only account of the years before any document

stops.name: Zona oeste, the neighborhood schools
stops.date_confidence: undated, placed before 2012 by her own periodization of formal training; the interview gives no year for the neighborhood schools and no name for any of them. Same conventional Morón stand-in as the previous stop.
stops.campa: In the west of the province the neighborhood schools of that period teach several dances at once, and a child is enrolled in all of them without choosing between them. She begins with clásico español and zapateo americano, the castanet and the shoe, then changes school and finds jazz. No academy, no conservatory, no audition, and no source anywhere names a single one of the schools. What survives of these years is one sentence she gives a camera some twenty years afterward: 'Siempre fui a escuelas de barrio. Yo me crié en el oeste, en provincia de Buenos Aires.'
stops.quote: Siempre fui a escuelas de barrio. Yo me crié en el oeste, en provincia de Buenos Aires.
suggested_refs: The neighborhood dance schools of the western Gran Buenos Aires, none of them named in any source

segments.name: A Record That Begins in the Middle

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, the formation she dates herself
stops.date_confidence: range given in her own words, 'más o menos desde el 2012 hasta el 2018'; the stop is placed at the opening of the range she states. No enrolment record, matriculation date or student file is reachable. Coordinate is the Nominatim geocode of Martín Rodríguez 444, La Boca, the Departamento de Artes del Movimiento of the UNA.
stops.campa: She dates her own formation, unprompted, from 2012 to 2018. Inside that range she is enrolled at the Departamento de Artes del Movimiento on Martín Rodríguez and also taking classes everywhere else: 'tomé 80,000 clases por fuera,' she says, a number that is a Rioplatense shrug and not a count. Eleven lines later she supplies the real figure, five or six classes a day with different teachers, ballet and contemporary and jazz stacked on top of one another. The degree she is working toward is a licenciatura in choreographic composition. It will take her until 2023 to finish it.
stops.quote: Así fue la formación, más o menos desde el 2012 hasta el 2018.
suggested_refs: The Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, UNA, Martín Rodríguez 444, La Boca

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, two teachers named
stops.date_confidence: no year is attached to either teacher anywhere; both are placed at the opening of the 2012-2018 formation range she gives. Litvak is independently corroborated by the 28 February 2026 NewsDigitales press profile, Mucio by nothing beyond the interview itself.
stops.campa: Two teachers survive into her account of the building. Gerardo Litvak in composition is the one who breaks what she later calls her snob phase: exacting, objective inside a subjective discipline, 'no se le escapa una.' Natalia Mucio in technique brings a total devotion to the room, an 'entrega total' that Massacesi qualifies in the same breath as 'innecesaria,' though welcome in a class. A press profile written fourteen years later names Litvak, independently, as instrumental to her development. Nobody in any source names a year for either of them.
stops.quote: Uno de los que me hizo cuestionarme muchas cosas es Gerardo Litvak en composición... Él detecta todo, como no se le escapa una, tiene una templanza.
suggested_refs: newsdigitales.com/nota/326577, the February 2026 press profile naming Litvak

stops.name: Buenos Aires, two videos uploaded in January
stops.date_confidence: upload dates verified with yt-dlp on the channel @emiliamassacesi4887: TrexXvZgLa8 on 15 January 2015 and 7u-GWhBkQvQ on 17 January 2015. stops.campa: The earliest trace of Emilia Massacesi that anyone outside her family can reach is two video files. On 15 January 2015 a clip titled 'Danza contemporánea' goes up on a YouTube channel bearing her name; two days later a second, titled 'Danza Contemporanea febrero 2015,' a month its own upload date contradicts. In both she is already dancing, on a fixed camera, in a room nobody has identified. Behind them there is nothing: no birth date in any reachable source, no birthplace, no first performance, no school photograph, no programme.

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, the UNA company under Grinstein
stops.date_confidence: attested: the alternativateatral ficha for Laboratori de Cruce is dated 2015 and lists Roxana Grinstein as director with Massacesi in a twenty-five-dancer cast; her own interview independently gives 2015 as the year she entered the company. The interview's auto-captions render the director's name 'Greenstein,' which is a caption artifact and is corrected here.
stops.campa: In 2015 she enters the student company of the Universidad Nacional de las Artes, directed by Roxana Grinstein, with guest choreographers rotating through it. The company dances Laboratori de Cruce in the Jardín Botánico, twenty-five names on the cast list, choreography by Ana Frenkel and Emanuel Ludueña, music by Tonolec. She stays three years. 'De lunes a sábado, de 9 a 1,' she says of the schedule, which is to say the whole of her waking life. The same year she appears in two further productions, one of them inside the Teatro Colón.
stops.quote: En el 2015 fue que entré a la compañía de la UNA, que es la compañía de estudiantes
stops.quote_source: Emilia Massacesi, NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript, line 285

Castadiva and the UNA company are the two hitos she names when she is asked about her formation, and she names no others. Then, on camera years later, addressing a woman who is not in the room: 'Moni, la amo. Te amo, Moni. Gran maestra.'

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, the thesis defended at last
stops.date_confidence: her own account: coursework finished around 2018 or 2019, thesis completed and defended in 2023, with about two and a half years of consistent pole practice behind her by that point. No month is given, no thesis title is stated anywhere, and no copy of the thesis has been located.
stops.campa: She finishes coursework around 2018 or 2019 and then the thesis takes years. She defends it in 2023 and becomes Licenciada en Composición Coreográfica of the Universidad Nacional de las Artes. By the day of the defence she has been training in pole consistently for about two and a half years, in a discipline that no part of the licenciatura acknowledges exists. She holds a degree in composing dance, and is at that moment composing something the degree has no vocabulary for. The thesis title appears in no reachable source.

segments.name: The Pandemic, the Reel, and the Pole

stops.name: Zona oeste, a reel of a Russian dancer
stops.date_confidence: 'yo hago pol desde el 2020,' her own words; the move west and the unemployment are hers as well, undated within the year. The pin is the same conventional Morón stand-in used for her childhood stops, since she names only the province.
stops.campa: The pandemic sends her back west, to the province, without work. Somewhere in that year an Instagram reel of a Russian exotic dancer crosses her feed and she says the recognition was immediate: es por acá. 'Yo hago pol desde el 2020,' she says, and gives no month for it. The geography inverts as she goes. In concert dance everything is in the capital and the province is its suburb; in pole, by her account, the province has the larger scene and the capital the smaller one.
suggested_refs: The pole studios of the western Gran Buenos Aires, which she says outnumber the capital's

stops.name: Zona oeste, Clase Contempo and Estiramientos de Tardecita
stops.date_confidence: eight videos titled Clase Contempo and two titled Estiramientos de Tardecita are dated to August and September 2020 on her YouTube channel, verified with yt-dlp; the recording location is not identifiable in any of them, and the pin follows her stated residence that year rather than any visible room.
stops.campa: Between August and September of that same year her channel fills with recorded classes: eight videos titled Clase Contempo, two more called Estiramientos de Tardecita, a contemporary teacher filming herself for students she cannot be in a room with. No clean handoff, then, no theatre put down before pole is picked up. Her upload dates and her own account of when she started put both inside the same two months of the same year. Nothing in any of the ten videos identifies the room she is filming in.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a room of the alienated
stops.date_confidence: undated statement of reasons, given retrospectively in a 2026 interview and placed at the year of the break she is explaining. The phrase 'una de alienados' appears identically in the long interview and in the short clip cut from it; the transcript is machine-generated and garbled at this point, so the wording is approximate.
stops.campa: Two pressures converge and she names both. The first is arithmetic: few companies, many dancers, no dance law in force, and no way to live on contemporary dance in Argentina without self-managing everything. The second is harder to argue with. The work had stopped reaching her as a spectator, and she was sitting in rooms where everyone agreed and nothing was at risk. Against that she sets what she found in erotic dance, 'provocación e incomodidad,' and says she knew intuitively that the way out ran through it.
stops.quote: Sentí que la danza contemporánea me dejó de hablar como espectadora... como que sentí que estábamos como en una de alienados.
stops.quote_source: Emilia Massacesi, NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript, lines 497-498; identical wording in the NewsDigitales Shorts clip
suggested_refs: The NewsDigitales Shorts clip, which carries the same sentence in shorter form

At the Teatro Libre in Bogotá she dances Kitsune Kitten Fantasy at Exotic Generation Latinoamérica and takes silver in the Flow category, plus the prize for best choreography. That choreography medal is the object she holds up to a camera four years later and calls, dryly, her real university degree. A press summary attaches the Colombian choreography prize instead to her later folk-dance duet; her own account does not, and the two versions are left standing side by side.

stops.name: Teatro del Globo, the Naruto routine
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio, which records bronze in the Pole-up High Heels Pro category; the interview and the February 2026 press profile independently give the same story and call it her second competition, with third place. Bronze and third place are consistent, but whether the interview's 'second competition' is this event or another is not settled by any source.
stops.campa: Her second competition, at the Teatro del Globo. She is deep in Naruto at the time and builds the routine around an exotic-dancer version of the character: orange costume, blonde braids, and total commitment to a premise she describes in hindsight as 'no es una buena idea. Pero sí sucedió.' The portfolio records it as bronze in the Pole-up High Heels Pro category; she and a press profile written four years later both call it third place, and both tell the story the same way without her prompting it. People still greet her as Naruto.

A Colombian medal for choreography. A trophy shaped like a flying saucer. Later, a runner-up sash.

stops.date_confidence: the date is the upload date of her own video, 'Exotic Generation Argentina 2023 - Em Port - Hard - tercer puesto LA TRAMPA ES LEY' (TtjBbHk7VL8), verified with yt-dlp; the performance itself is undated and no venue is named in any source, so the pin is the city-level anchor. A press summary calls the partner 'Calu'; her own voice says 'Caru' throughout, and the contradiction is left open.
stops.campa: At Exotic Generation Argentina 2023 she and her friend Caru dance a chacarera exótica in the Hard category: a dúo lésbico gauchesco, Caru the gaucha and Massacesi the china, Caru also playing bombo mid-performance, both of them in twenty-three-centimetre heels. The music is a mash of Chaqueño Palavecino's La trampa es ley with a Lit Killah remix. The crowd starts applauding at the first bars of the folk original, before the remix arrives at all, because, she says, 'es algo que está en nuestro ADN.' Third place.

stops.campa: Exotic Generation Spain, Old School Pro, two videos on the channel and no other trace anywhere. Old School is the third of the styles she lays out on camera: not the fluid undulating flow associated with Eva Bembo, not the grounded and forceful hard style associated with Olga Koda, but 'el del club, como el Full Hotness, seductor,' the one that comes from the room the pole came from. She crosses an ocean to compete in the oldest category of a very young discipline. The title names a country and no city.

stops.date_confidence: current-state description from the 2026 interview, undated within the year beyond the broadcast window; the move to a larger space is stated as intention, not as fact, and the instructor count of three to four with two more incoming is hers.
stops.campa: Almagro Exotic Club teaches pole sport, pole exotic and floor work, with three or four instructors and two more coming, in a space she says is already too small. 'Somos un zoológico,' she says of it: civilians beside artists beside pole people, baby and challenge and professional levels sharing one room, no dress code, no single acceptable body. Building it meant confronting her own prejudice, she says, contemporary-dance training having no place for surgically altered bodies or for botox.
